goals: mechanistic: quantify how water partitioning (ET vs surface runoff vs sub-surface drainage/recharge, plus snow storage/melt) varies with elevation across the Bow headwaters
validation: benchmark simulated partitioning/snow/streamflow against in-domain observations
drivers_to_resolve: elevation (acting through orographic precip, temperature lapse, snowpack)

model_choice.rationale: ELM single-column resolves the vertical water/energy/snow balance the question targets; but the elevation driver depends on elevation-resolved forcing the stack lacks outside CONUS.

answerable: soil-texture control on partitioning (ET / surface runoff / drainage) under a single forcing — but this is NOT the elevation signal requested

not_answerable.aspect: elevation-resolved precipitation and temperature (orographic gradient across 2200 m relief)
not_answerable.why: domain is in Canada; NLDAS-2 is CONUS-only, so forcing falls back to Qian T62 ~1.9deg, which is NOT elevation-resolved — the whole basin draws essentially one climate

not_answerable.aspect: elevation-resolved snowpack / rain-snow transition (dominant partitioning control in this alpine basin)
not_answerable.why: snow response is driven by the elevation-resolved temperature/precip that the fallback forcing cannot supply
SNOTEL is a US-only network; no in-domain snow observations are in the stack
not_answerable.needs: Canadian snow-observation ingest (ECCC / provincial snow pillows)

not_answerable.aspect: validation of streamflow against ECCC gauges
not_answerable.why: ECCC gauges are not ingested in the stack, AND single-column ELM produces no routed streamflow without an aggregation/routing step

sampling_strategy.approach: stratified (elevation x soil) — NOTE: elevation strata cannot isolate the intended climate signal under uniform fallback forcing; recorded as a degraded fallback only

classes: dominant SSURGO/native texture per band (as resolved by expander)

sampling_strategy.n_justification: 3 elevation bands x 2 dominant soil classes spans the resolvable soil heterogeneity; kept minimal because the primary elevation/climate axis is NOT resolvable, so a larger elevation sweep would be blind. This is a fallback soil-control design, not the requested elevation-resolved experiment.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: oversample valley-bottom / riparian corridors where soil-moisture and drainage response is strongest; distribute remainder across the elevation bands to document soil variation only
sampling_strategy.replication: none — until elevation-resolved forcing exists, replication adds cost without resolving the target driver

sampling_plan.reason: characterizes soil control on partitioning at low elevation under single fallback forcing (elevation signal NOT resolved)
spans mid-basin soil texture; would host rain-snow transition IF elevation-resolved forcing were available (it is not)
high-elevation soil endmember; snow-dominated partitioning here cannot be resolved without elevation-resolved forcing

validation_design.comparison: none possible — SNOTEL is US-only; would require Canadian snow-obs ingest
none possible — ECCC gauges not in stack, and single-column ELM has no routed streamflow

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: single fallback forcing (Qian T62), native/SSURGO soil per column — NOTE elevation NOT resolved by forcing

requires_capabilities.capability: non-CONUS elevation-resolved forcing (Canadian gridded product or orographic downscaling)
requires_capabilities.why: elevation acts through precip/temperature/snow; the requested elevation-resolved partitioning is meaningless under uniform ~1.9deg Qian forcing
requires_capabilities.blocks: the entire primary question (elevation-resolved partitioning and snow)

requires_capabilities.capability: Canadian snow-observation ingest (ECCC / provincial snow pillows)
requires_capabilities.why: SNOTEL does not cover Canada; snow validation needs in-domain data
in-domain gauges exist but are not in the stack
single-column ELM produces no integrated streamflow for gauge comparison
requires_capabilities.blocks: streamflow validation even after gauge ingest

requires_capabilities.why: any recharge/water-table partitioning target needs initialized slow states

assumptions: Domain lies fully outside CONUS, so NLDAS is unavailable and forcing defaults to Qian T62 (~1.9deg, not elevation-resolved).
'ECCC gauges (not in stack)' means present in reality but not ingestible by the current framework.
Dominant soil classes per elevation band will be resolved by the downstream expander from gridded soil rasters.
The fallback 6-column soil-control design is offered ONLY to show what the stack can do; it does not answer the user's elevation-resolved question.
open_questions: Is a Canadian elevation-resolved forcing dataset (e.g., RDRS/ERA5-downscaled) available to ingest? Without it this question cannot be answered.
Can ECCC gauge and Canadian snow-pillow records be ingested to enable any validation?
Would the user accept a reframed CONUS analog basin (e.g., a Rocky Mountain headwaters within NLDAS coverage) to study the same elevation-partitioning mechanism?
